utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session, and I'd like to ask the Registrar to call the case first, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have the appearances for the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Counsel. For the Prosecution, Chester Stamp and Ekkehard Withopf, with Kimberly Fleming as the case manager.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of General Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, Defence counsel Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and Mirna Milanovic, legal assistant. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. For the Defence of Mr. Kubura, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic and our legal assistant, Mr. Nermin Mulalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Chamber would like to say good morning to all those present, to the Prosecution, the Defence, the accused, and of course the other members of the staff of this Tribunal. Before we proceed from where we left off yesterday - that is to say, the testimony of the witness we're examining - I should like to address two points. One concerns the translation and that matter was raised yesterday. In the meantime, there was a meeting with the Registry to discuss the matter, and according to the information I have been given, I should like to inform you of the following. It seems that at the beginning, the Defence gave the CLSS - that is to say, the translation service - 3.000 pages to deal with for translation. Now, when faced with 3.000 pages, the CLSS asked the Defence to tell them which portions had priority for translation purposes, but it appears that there was no precise answer given, no response from them. Now, as we have such a lot of translation, they managed to translate 1.300 pages of those 3.000, which leaves 1.700 pages to translate. In view of the importance of this issue, the Registrar has considered that all the material produced by the Defence, the destination of which is the Tribunal, will be translated. So there are two types of documents in question. They are either exhibits you wish to tender, and as we said, you must present them well in advance to the CLSS for translation - or the other types of documents were documents you would be using in the cross-examination but which will not be tendered into evidence during the proceedings. So having received those guidelines, that seems to be quite different than what was envisaged thus far. So what was decided went in the direction of meeting the Defence's requirements. Now, concerning the aspects that I should like to call financial or budgetary, this is how we stand. It appears that a certain sum of money has been allotted to the Defence and that that sum of money in bulk includes costs and expenditure for translations, and so the Defence may use a portion of that money for translation purposes. Of course, that doesn't resolve the question that you raised with respect to additional documents. So that is what I'm able to tell you today, and perhaps that will be enough for the Defence. Perhaps we need to look into the matter additionally. So I think that you should contact the relevant Registry services to settle the matter once and for all. Of course, in the extent to which the Chamber can be of assistance and needs translations of documents in the two languages are the ones that you have in B/C/S and provide in B/C/S. So that's the first point I wanted to make. Would anybody like to take the floor to discuss the matter further, or would you need time for thought? Yes. You have the floor, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we really do not wish to burden the Trial Chamber with matters which we know we'll have to deal with and resolve with the Registry; however, as we depend on the translated documents and the defence of our clients depends on the translation of those documents, we did have to address you, the Trial Chamber. Mr. President, in November -- you came to this Tribunal in November. In November of the previous year - that is to say, one year previously - we put forward a series of written motions because we had experience from before and knew that we could be faced with a difficult situation. Yes, we will continue our discussion and dialogue with the Registry, but I have to tell you that it is very difficult for the Defence to give the CLSS documents from one day to the next or one week to the next which it needs to use for the witness in hand, because we have received witnesses for just the next seven days. So this is a very tight deadline. And the translation service, even with the best will in the world, will not be able to translate all the material. So it was for these reasons that we considered that it would be a good idea for a just trial to be able to discuss this matter with the Registry, to draw their attention to the fact that we would use the hours more flexibly that we were given for translation purposes in the first place: For us to avoid situations of this kind, the ones we face. And secondly, I'm not qualified sufficiently to say whether in the lump sum that we were given that this envisages translation too. I took part in discussions which brought about this system of the lump sum, and nobody mentioned the costs of translation within the lump sum, but legal assistants -- rather, case managers, investigators, and other staff and personnel which enables the Defence team to perform its function in the courtroom. However, I'd like to extend my gratitude to you for taking up the matter. We shall do our best to give the -- provide the Registry with the most important documents, but I must say once again, Your Honours, in view of the experience we've gained over the past year, these problems will crop up and they will accrue. So I hope you will understand the situation and do your best to help the Defence in performing its duties. Thank you. I don't know whether it would be necessary, but my learned colleague, Mr. Stephane Bourgon, took part in all these negotiations. He's written hundreds of pages, attended many, many meetings. And if the Trial Chamber feels that we need to say more on the matter, we are, of course, always ready to provide you with further information. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, madam. What about Mr. Kubura's Defence? Would they like to say anything on the subject?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have no further comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I should just like to inform the Defence that for practical purposes, in order to try and solve the difficulties facing us, that the Defence is facing, that if you have a document in B/C/S which has not been translated, can you always tell us, because we have realised that some documents have been integrated international procedure with respect to instructions and information on fact. So if you're producing documents for the cross-examination, of course the Prosecution does not know which those are, nor does the Trial Chamber. But the practical decision that we have made is that you should tell us, place your confidence in us, and tell us the contents of the document, because as the vehicles of justice, of course you're not going to give a different interpretation with respect to the contents of the document. So we'd like to know the contents of the document, and provisionally such a document could be introduced into the proceedings and marked for identification, been given a provisional number. The document would then be sent off to the translation service for translation, and then there would be a final tendering into evidence once the document has been translated. This would perhaps allow us to solve part of the difficulty you're facing. Not all of them, of course, but a part of the difficulty, get round the matter that way. So I think it would be useful if you once again contact the Registry for us to be able to proceed as quickly as possible. Of course, as you know full well, if your difficulties prove to be insurmountable, it would of course be possible for you to file a motion to us about that and with respect to the equality of arms that you would like to see prevail. We'll see what we'll decide in that case. Now, with respect to the second point, in the coming hour we shall be making our ruling known to you concerning the motion that was filed with respect to modifying our previous oral ruling and the certificate of appeal. So in the course of the day, we can expect to have that correction in the form. And the Chamber partially confirms its decision and ruling and certifies the appeal made by the Prosecution. So the Appeals Chamber will have to give its ruling with respect to the matter. As the Appeals Chamber will be taking a certain amount of time -- but in view of the urgency of the matter, I think they'll be able to give us a ruling shortly -- the Trial Chamber would like to say that we should take it on a case-by-case basis, if other cases arise, but having respect for the oral ruling that you have all been apprised of, and including what I've said here today. Now, if we have no further matters to attend to, let us move on and we'll be in private session. I'd like to ask Madam Registrar to see to the practical ways of doing that and to tell me when we are in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session. I'd like to ask the Prosecution now whether they have a new witness for us or whether we've exhausted the witnesses for this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. WITHOPF
utterances.text: Your Honour, as already announced yesterday, there's no further witness available for today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me address all parties. Nobody wishes to raise any matters at this point? If not, I adjourn the meeting for today. It is 10.30 a.m., which coincides with our usual break. The Judges of this Trial Chamber schedule the next meeting on Monday, the 12th of January. We'll see you all back. I think we're having an afternoon session on the 12th of January, although I haven't received confirmation yet. So we meet again in three weeks' time. In the meantime, I should like to wish one and all a happy festive season for the end of the year for yourselves and your families and we'll reconvene on the 12th of January, 2004.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on the 12th day of January, 2004, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 10.28 a.m.,
